what_was_missing: Nothing to move: guard-hook.mjs and selftest.mjs were already flat in tcb/, and tcb/scripts/ did not exist (no folder to delete).

guard-hook.mjs was complete and already flat (Bash grammar `node tcb/<n>.mjs` or `node "<root>/tcb/<n>.mjs"`, sibling check from import.meta.url). It was left unchanged. A read-only check through the lane against the build root gave the spec's answer on 17 decisions (tcb-node allow; tcb/scripts path, lib, nosuch and `;` denied as bash-pattern; README read allowed; lib.mjs read denied; .git write-protected; Claude.MD write-claude; Agent checker allowed and reader denied; helper checker without batch.json denied; helper reader in a coordinator folder denied as helper-type; WebFetch denied; a throwing io gave internal). As a process it gave exit 2 with one `[guard-hook] deny` line.

Role files were complete and consistent. All 11 profiles pass the profile schema. Every settings/<role>.json parses after substitution, its hook command is `"{node}" "{root}/tcb/guard-hook.mjs" --root "{root}" --role <role>` (task roles add --task/--epoch), its allow rules use only tools_allow tools and its deny list holds every tools_deny entry. No file names tcb/scripts. agents/reader.md has `tools: WebSearch, WebFetch` and checker.md has `tools: Read`; each body is byte-equal to its brief. None of these was changed.
selftest.mjs needed the no-burst redesign (done; see deviations). Its spec was rewritten to match.
deviations_from_the_spec: selftest --jobs: the default is now 1, not max(1, min(8, cpus-2, (free_mb - reserve_mb)/200)). Only 1 or 2 is accepted; any other value (0, 3, 4...) exits 66 usage. reserve_mb is no longer read, and free memory and the CPU count no longer change anything. Old T6 used --jobs 4 and must use --jobs 2.

selftest makes no copy of the script folder. Each case spawns the live script `<root>/tcb/<script>.mjs`, with cwd and --root at the case root. The case root's tcb/ holds data files only: schemas/, profiles/, settings/, agents/, briefs/, thresholds.json (with overrides), cost-inputs.json, denylist.txt and README.md. It holds no .mjs, no fixtures/ and no test/. In a stub, process.argv[1] is `<root>/tcb/<name>.mjs`. A stub that expects a sibling script under the case root finds none. Test stubs must sit flat in `<root>/tcb/<name>.mjs`, not `<root>/tcb/scripts/`.

A case root is made just before its case runs and removed as soon as the case is judged, no longer at the end of the run. At most --jobs case roots exist at once. --keep-failed still keeps failing roots, and stdout result.kept lists them.

After every case, treeSha(<root>/tcb/) is compared with t0. The first change stops the run: no later case starts, result not_run, exit 2, reason tcb-changed with detail {before, after, case}. The final t1 check remains. In selftest.json, `cases` lists only the cases that ran, and stdout result.not_started lists the cases a stop kept from starting.

New not-run causes. (a) After a case child exits, its stdout and stderr must close within 3 s. A pipe still open means a descendant is alive: the case fails with why 'left-process', the run stops, and the result is not_run with reason case-left-process (exit 2). (b) A timed-out child still alive case_timeout + 30 s after its kill stops the run with reason case-not-ended (not_run). Before, it was abandoned and the run went on. selftest still never kills anything but a timed-out child's verified tree.

On timeout the kill is awaited before anything else happens. The next case in that slot starts only after the child has exited, its pipes have closed, the server has closed and any kill has finished. The `close` event is captured from spawn time (the old waitClose could miss a close emitted in the same tick as exit).

watch-case-loops is stricter. A watch case must carry both --once and --no-intake, and neither --alarm nor --intake. Before, --once alone, --intake, or --alarm with --sleep-ms below the case timeout all passed. Reason: without --no-intake, --once may spawn the detached intake. status and handover have one-shot modes only and get no extra check.
reasons on a not_run result list every not-run cause (tcb-changed first), then failed checks, then case-failed entries. Before, only one not-run cause was listed.

The selftest spec now uses the flat layout throughout (tcb/<name>.mjs). Behaviours were changed or added: T5 (kill ends both before the next case starts), T5b (new watch rule; nothing spawned, no tmp/), T5c (the case root's tcb/ has no .mjs; the stub's argv[1] is the live path), T5e (new: one case root at a time by default, at most 2 with --jobs 2, --jobs 3 and 0 are 66), T5f (new: left-process / case-left-process / not_started), T6 (--jobs 2 vs 1), T8 (detail names the case; no later case ran).

selftest T5 risk for the join stage: if killOwnTree misses the stub's grandchild and that grandchild inherited the stub's stdout/stderr, the run now ends not_run with case-left-process (exit 2) and not with a completed run. This only happens when the kill really failed.

guard-hook (unchanged, but different from its spec text, which still says tcb/scripts). The coordinator's Bash/PowerShell grammar is `node tcb/<n>.mjs` (cwd = root) or `node "<root>/tcb/<n>.mjs"`, so `node tcb/scripts/status.mjs` is now bash-pattern. The script must exist beside guard-hook.mjs (import.meta.url), not under `<root>/tcb/scripts/`. The settings hook command is `"{node}" "{root}/tcb/guard-hook.mjs" ...`. The coordinator allow rule is `Bash(node tcb/*)`. guard-hook T5 and T14 must use these forms.

guard-hook additions already in the draft (kept): writes are always refused under tcb/, sealed/, review-in/, .claude/, run/, store/, .git/ even when thresholds lists fewer; a Glob/Grep whose search path is a parent of sealed/ is refused; path-unresolvable also covers 8.3 short names (~digit), alternate data streams, wildcard characters, drive-relative and rooted-without-drive paths; profiles may carry schema_version 1; reader and checker given as --role take no --task/--epoch.
lib_change_requests: audit.mjs (U4a): `const NODE_PREFIX = 'node tcb/scripts/'` (line 34) still names the old layout. guard-hook allows only `node tcb/<n>.mjs`, so audit should use 'node tcb/' (excluding lib) so the hook and audit enforce the same grammar.
lib.mjs: paths(root).scripts is still j('tcb', 'scripts') (line 436). For the flat layout it should be j('tcb').
tcb/README.md (U5c), line 8: `node tcb/scripts/<name>.mjs` should be `node tcb/<name>.mjs`.

spec/guard-hook.mjs.md (not writable by this stage): steps 12 and T5, the settings command and `Bash(node tcb/scripts/*)` should read tcb/<n>.mjs, {root}/tcb/guard-hook.mjs and Bash(node tcb/*). CONTRACT §3.21 and §5 say the same old paths.

Tests (join stage): guard-hook.test.mjs and selftest.test.mjs both reference tcb/scripts (stubs, the hook path, Bash commands) and must move to the flat layout and to the selftest changes listed under deviations_from_the_spec.

Fixture cases (owned by the units that test each script): case.json folders exist for only 12 scripts (admit, audit, certify, compare, cost, gate, promote, protocol-freeze, render, replace, stop, tms). A full `selftest run` on the build tree will fail the static check no-fixtures for check-queue, commit, fsck, guard-hook, handover, harvest, seed, selftest, snap, status, watch and witness. Watch cases, when written, must carry --once and --no-intake.

profiles/coordinator.json: per the spec table, its tools_allow should also hold the host's session tools as `<prefix>*` entries. The owner must add those; without them the hook refuses the coordinator's session tools with tool-not-allowed.
not_testable_without_the_app: needs-app 1: the harness runs guard-hook before every tool call (helpers too), passes agent_type, and honours exit 2. A hook timeout or a node that fails to start lets the call through.
needs-app 2: user-level denies bind every session, and the `//` absolute form works on Windows.
needs-app 3: a session in wt/<task>-e<e>/ obeys that folder's settings and agent files and no ancestor's.
needs-app 7 and 11: real transcripts carry a refusal as an error result with the hook's stderr; the canary session's refusals as read by `selftest canary`.
Whether the permission rule `Bash(node tcb/*)` matches the coordinator's commands as intended under the harness's rule syntax.
open_points: The reader profile keeps tools_allow WebSearch, WebFetch, ToolSearch, StructuredOutput, as the spec table says. The reader agent file holds exactly WebSearch and WebFetch. If 'a reader holds web search and web fetch only' is meant for the profile too, ToolSearch should be dropped. StructuredOutput is how a reader returns [reader-result], so removing it would break harvest's input.

Leftover-process detection relies on pipes. A descendant started detached with stdio 'ignore' is not seen after its parent exits. Seeing it would need one process list per case (one PowerShell per case, sequential). Today the only script that starts such a process is watch --once without --no-intake, and the static check refuses that case.

No smoke of the new selftest design was run. This stage may write only its own files, so it built no temp run root, and the brief forbade a smoke of the old design. What was checked: node --check of both scripts through the lane, plus the read-only guard-hook and role-file check described above. The first real exercise will be the join stage's tests.
watch.mjs was changed by another agent while this stage ran (its intake now finds siblings from import.meta.url). selftest relies only on watch's --once/--no-intake flags.
